name: Agent security hardening & 'lethal trifecta' review for SMEs
customer: SMEs/teams adopting personal agents (OpenClaw-type), MCP connectors, coding agents
problem: Agents combine private data, untrusted content and outbound actions; exposed instances, malicious skills and MCP CVEs documented; prompt injection unsolved
workaround: Ban agents (shadow use continues); rely on vendor defaults; generic pentest
value: Fixed-scope review: inventory of agents/MCP servers/skills, permission and secret scoping, sandboxing, approval gates, logging; maps to OWASP ASI and Five-Eyes guidance
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: large exposure counts and malicious skills (S014), government restrictions (S013), joint government guidance (S051). INFERRED: SMEs lack in-house expertise.
distribution: IT MSP partnerships; security community talks; insurer/broker referrals
operating_burden: Medium–high: fast-moving threat landscape, liability for advice
competitors: Security consultancies, MSSPs, vendor security features (Entra Agent ID, guardrail products)
defensibility: Low–medium: expertise; checklists can be copied
failure: SMEs do not prioritise until an incident; trust barrier for a new provider
invalidation: Target SMEs report no agent use beyond vendor-managed copilots
experiment: (Needs approval) Publish free self-assessment checklist; measure requests for paid review
next_action: Draft checklist (in paper appendix) mapped to OWASP ASI01–10
why: evidence: incidents and guidance well documented (S014,S051); pain high when incident occurs; competition from established security firms; risk: advice liability

name: Coding-agent enablement & measurement for small dev teams
problem: Coding agents are widely used (66% of AI users) but productivity gains are hard to measure; governance and cost controls immature
workaround: Each developer self-configures; vendor seat licences without measurement
value: AGENTS.md/repo conventions, CI guardrails, permission & secret policy, cost dashboards, before/after measurement design
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: high usage (S062), large vendor revenue (S053), 32% declined purchases because buildable in-house (S004). INFERRED: managers want measurable ROI.
competitors: Vendor solution engineers (free), large consultancies, internal champions
failure: Vendors provide enablement free; teams self-serve
invalidation: CTOs report no measurement need or no budget for enablement
experiment: (Needs approval) 10 CTO interviews on measurement pain
metric: Share willing to pay for measured pilot
next_action: Draft measurement protocol based on METR design lessons
why: evidence: adoption well documented (S062,S053); competition: vendors give enablement away

name: Independent evaluation & outcome-audit for support agents
customer: Companies running AI support agents (built or bought) with ≥5k conversations/month
economic_buyer: Head of customer support / CX; CFO when billed per outcome
problem: Vendors bill per 'outcome' with generous definitions (e.g., no further help requested = outcome); LLM judges overestimate quality 2–3x; resolution rate is the dominant cost driver
workaround: Trust vendor dashboards; ad-hoc manual spot checks; CSAT surveys
value: Human-calibrated sampling of transcripts, true-resolution rate, wrongful-resolution and policy-violation rate, invoice reconciliation vs per-outcome billing, regression evals on model changes
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: outcome-based pricing in market (S071); LLM-judge overestimation documented (S037); quality reversal at Klarna (S072); VC funding in eval/observability (S073). INFERRED: buyers of per-outcome pricing need verification.
distribution: Partnerships with support-tool consultancies; content on resolution economics; CX communities
conversion: Paid pilot audit of one month of transcripts
setup_cost: Low–medium: rubric, sampling tooling, data-processing agreement templates
operating_burden: Medium: human graders, data protection obligations
dependencies: Customer willing to share transcripts (GDPR DPA)
competitors: Braintrust, Arize, LangSmith (tools, not independent audit); vendor QA features; BPO QA teams
defensibility: Medium: independence + calibrated benchmarks across vendors
failure: Buyers satisfied with vendor-reported metrics; data-sharing friction too high
invalidation: Audits find vendor-reported resolution within ±5 pts of human-judged across several customers
experiment: (Needs approval) Offer 3 discounted audits; compare human-judged vs vendor-reported resolution
metric: Gap between reported and audited resolution; willingness to renew
threshold: Gap ≥10 pts in ≥2 of 3 and ≥1 converts to monthly
next_action: Write audit rubric from OWASP/Five-Eyes guidance and RLI human-judging method
open_questions: How common is per-outcome billing in EU; legal basis to process transcripts
why: evidence: mechanisms documented (S037,S071) but no buyer demand observed; pain: resolution dominates cost (CALC L36); wtp: plausible via invoice savings; competition: tools exist but not independent audits

name: Agent-readiness service for non-Shopify merchants
customer: Small/mid e-commerce merchants on WooCommerce, Magento, custom stacks (EU/Baltics first)
problem: AI assistants increasingly send shoppers and run discovery via structured feeds and protocols (ACP, UCP); agents choose using product text, position and endorsements; merchants outside Shopify/large retailers lack the feeds, policies and data quality to be selected
workaround: Do nothing; rely on Google Merchant Center feed; generic SEO agency
value: Audit + implement agent-readable catalog (UCP/ACP feeds), product-description quality, agent access policy (Cloudflare/robots/signed agents), checkout handoff, and measurement of AI-referred traffic
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: AI-referred US retail traffic +393% YoY Q1 2026, converting 42% better (S031); large retailers integrating ACP/UCP (S023,S025). INFERRED: smaller non-Shopify merchants will want parity. No merchant has been asked.
distribution: E-commerce platform partner directories, local e-commerce associations, agencies white-label
pricing: Fixed-fee audit €1.5–3k; implementation €3–10k; optional monthly monitoring €200–500 (HYPOTHESIS)
operating_burden: Medium: protocol churn requires continuous learning
dependencies: UCP/ACP specs and Google/OpenAI merchant programs remaining open to mid-size merchants
competitors: Shopify native Agentic Storefronts (substitute for Shopify merchants); feed-management SaaS; SEO/GEO agencies
defensibility: Low–medium: know-how and case studies; becomes commoditised as platforms automate
platform_risk: High: OpenAI already pivoted checkout once (S025); platforms may bypass merchants or automate onboarding
failure: Platforms make onboarding self-serve for all merchants; AI-referred traffic stays <2% of sales so merchants don't pay
invalidation: Merchant interviews show AI-referred revenue immaterial; or platform self-serve tools achieve parity in <1 day
experiment: (Needs approval to contact merchants) 15 discovery calls with Baltic/EU merchants using a free 'agent visibility' report generated from public pages
metric: Share of calls converting to paid audit at stated price
next_action: Build public 'agent visibility' checklist from UCP/ACP specs; draft report template (no outreach until approved)
open_questions: Size of AI-referred revenue for EU SMB merchants; UCP availability in EU
why: evidence: traffic & protocol adoption observed, SMB pain inferred (S031,S023); pain: medium—traffic share still small; wtp: unknown; access: reachable locally; feasibility/cost: services, no capital; competition: Shopify substitute; risk: high platform churn (S025)

name: MCP connector build & migration for vertical SaaS
customer: Vertical/regional SaaS vendors (accounting, booking, logistics) without agent interfaces
problem: Agents reach services through tools; MCP is the de-facto tool interface but the 2026-07-28 spec is breaking (stateless, auth changes); small vendors lack capacity
workaround: No agent interface; rely on browser automation by users' agents (fragile, ToS conflicts)
value: Design, build, secure (OAuth/CIMD), test and maintain an MCP server + A2A agent card; registry listing
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: >10k MCP servers (S034), SDK downloads (S033) show supply-side activity; INFERRED: smaller vendors want to be reachable by agents.
distribution: Direct to SaaS vendors; MCP community; partner with API-management firms
competitors: In-house teams, API-management vendors auto-generating MCP from OpenAPI, dev agencies, coding agents themselves
defensibility: Low: coding agents can generate servers; value is in security/ops
failure: Auto-generation becomes good enough; vendors don't see agent traffic
invalidation: Vendors report no customer requests for agent access
experiment: (Needs approval) Interview 10 regional SaaS vendors about customer requests for agent access
metric: Share with ≥1 customer request in last 6 months
next_action: Prepare reference MCP server template compliant with 2026-07-28 spec (local, no publication)
open_questions: Monetisation path for SaaS vendor from agent access
why: evidence: protocol adoption strong (S034), buyer pull unverified; competition: commoditising quickly via code generation

name: EU AI Act Art. 50 + agent governance starter kit for SMEs
customer: EU SMEs deploying chat/voice/email agents that interact with people
problem: Art. 50 disclosure duties apply since 2 Aug 2026 incl. AI agents; governance frameworks (Singapore, Five Eyes) expect accountability, logging and human oversight; SMEs lack templates
workaround: Ignore; ad-hoc disclaimers; expensive law firms
value: Templates and implementation: disclosure patterns, agent inventory, risk bounding, human-approval policy, logging retention, incident playbook; referral to lawyers for legal opinion
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: obligations in force with fines up to €15m/3% (S074). INFERRED: SME demand for templates.
distribution: Chambers of commerce, accountants, DPO networks; online template shop
dependencies: Must avoid unauthorised legal advice; legal review of templates
competitors: Law firms, GRC SaaS, free Commission guidance, generic AI-policy templates
failure: SMEs see disclosure as trivial (one sentence) and won't pay; enforcement invisible
invalidation: Regulators issue free comprehensive templates; no enforcement signals by 2027
experiment: (Needs approval) Landing page with kit outline; measure pre-orders
next_action: Map Art. 50 + Singapore 4 dimensions to a one-page checklist (paper appendix)
why: evidence: rules in force (S074); pain: low for simple disclosure; wtp: low; feasibility high

name: Hardened managed personal-agent setup for professionals
customer: Solo professionals and small teams wanting an always-on personal agent
problem: Open-source personal agents are popular but insecure by default; subscription-credential misuse leads to bans; costs can spike with long loops
workaround: DIY install; vendor assistants (ChatGPT/Claude apps with scheduled tasks); not using agents
value: Installed-for-you agent with sandbox, API-key billing, spend caps, scoped connectors, backups, monthly check-up
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: 247k GitHub stars (S013); bans of users on subscription OAuth (S016,S075). Stated (not revealed) WTP: 46% of Project Deal participants (S040).
operating_burden: High: per-customer support, security incidents liability
dependencies: Model vendors' ToS; open-source project stability
competitors: Vendor-native agents (ChatGPT agent, Claude Cowork) improving quickly; hosting providers' one-click templates
failure: Vendor-native assistants make DIY agents unnecessary; support burden kills margin
invalidation: Native assistants cover top-5 personal tasks with scheduling and connectors
experiment: (Needs approval) Offer 5 paid setups to warm contacts
next_action: None until owner decides; document hardened reference config
open_questions: Liability when an agent misuses customer accounts
why: evidence: popularity and incidents observed (S013,S014); wtp only stated (S040); competition from vendor-native agents; risk: ToS and liability

name: Agent-traffic policy & monetisation advisory for publishers
problem: Agent and training bots now blocked or monetised by default on major CDNs; decisions on allow/block/charge affect revenue and AI visibility
value: Traffic analysis, policy design, pay-per-crawl configuration, measurement
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: Cloudflare defaults (S019), agent blocks (S063). INFERRED: publishers need guidance.
competitors: Cloudflare/Akamai tools and docs; ad-tech consultancies
invalidation: Publishers report negligible agent-traffic revenue impact
why: evidence: defaults observed (S019); pain moderate; strong CDN-native substitutes

name: Pay-per-call data/API products sold to agents (MPP/x402)
customer: AI agents acting for owners, via agent payment rails
problem: Agents need fresh, specialised data/actions without subscriptions or account sign-up
workaround: Free web scraping (increasingly blocked by default), human-purchased subscriptions
value: Niche dataset/API (e.g., Baltic company registry enrichment, local regulations) priced per call, discoverable via MCP registries
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: rails live, but adjusted x402 volume ~$19M total and concentrated in ~4k buyers (S028). INFERRED: niche data could find buyers.
distribution: MCP registries, agent marketplaces, being chosen by agents (position/description effects S030)
dependencies: Legal right to resell data; rails stability
competitors: Free sources; large data vendors adding MCP
failure: Agents rarely pay; discovery depends on opaque model choices (S030)
invalidation: <100 paid calls/month after listing in major registries
experiment: (Needs approval for any spend) list a free-tier MCP data tool, measure call volume and source
next_action: Identify data with clear reuse rights
why: evidence: rails exist, demand thin (S028); selection by agents is unstable (S030)

name: Shopping-agent quality benchmark (consumer-facing media)
customer: Consumers choosing which agent/assistant to shop with; brands
problem: Agents differ in negotiation quality and biases, and users don't notice disadvantage (S040); position/sponsorship effects (S030)
value: Independent periodic tests of shopping agents on price, bias, manipulation-resistance
setup_cost: Medium: testing costs, careful ToS compliance
experiment: (Needs approval) publish one free study; measure inbound
why: evidence: behavioural research exists (S040,S030) but no buyer demand

name: Merchant evidence kit for agent-initiated disputes
problem: Liability for agent purchases unresolved; merchants bear disputes by default
value: Capture agent signatures (TAP/Web Bot Auth), mandates and confirmations as dispute evidence
why: evidence: liability gap documented only by vendor commentary (S066); volumes small

name: Spend controls & reconciliation for agent purchases (SMB finance)
problem: Agents can now pay (MPP, x402, Agent Pay, shared payment tokens) but liability, limits and reconciliation are immature
workaround: Shared company card in agent config; manual expense review
value: Per-agent virtual cards/wallets with mandates, limits, merchant allow-lists, receipts matching and anomaly alerts
demand_evidence: OBSERVED: rails launched (S024,S022), cost controls used by 38% of orgs for AI usage (S062). Volumes tiny (S028). INFERRED: need grows with agent purchasing.
competitors: Ramp, Brex, Stripe Issuing, Coinbase agent wallets, Mastercard/Visa agent programs
failure: Incumbent spend platforms ship agent cards first
invalidation: Agent purchasing volumes remain negligible through 2027
experiment: Desk research only until owner approves spend
why: evidence: rails exist but usage tiny (S028); cost/risk: regulated; competition: well-funded incumbents
